about: Usage stats and crash reports: everything Bridge AI can count and send. Both are on unless you turn them off (Settings › About & Updates), DO_NOT_TRACK=1 or BRIDGE_TELEMETRY=0 keeps them off, and the first time they're on a card says so. server/counts.js sends only the names and values here, and a test fails if the code counts any other; server/crashes.js sends only the report described under crashReports. Adding to either is a change to this file, in public.
endpointAbout: Where a week's report goes (HTTPS POST, JSON): the project's usage counts server, counts/worker.js in this repo, which keeps only weekly totals. Empty: there's nowhere to send them, so sharing isn't offered. A fork or a company sends them, and crash reports, to its own server instead with one setting, stats.url (counts/README.md, Running your own).

report.channel: the update channel: stable, or early for Early Access (pre-releases, for testers with a code from the project)
report.tester: on Early Access, who the code is for: the first name or nickname the project gave its tester (letters, numbers, spaces, dots, apostrophes and dashes; 32 at most); otherwise null
report.rollout: this computer's bucket for staged rollouts: a number from 0 to 99 picked once at random, shared with about one computer in a hundred, so a release out to 10% can be seen reaching buckets 0-9 first
report.osVersion: the OS's version: macOS 15.1, Windows 11 (26100), Ubuntu 24.04 (letters, numbers, spaces, dots, brackets; 40 at most)
report.chip: the chip's family, never the exact part: Apple M2 Pro, Intel Core i7, Intel Core Ultra 7, AMD Ryzen 7, Qualcomm Snapdragon, or 'other'
report.cores: CPU cores, as one of values.cores
report.install: desktop (the app), source (a clone) or docker
report.phones: phones paired with this computer, as one of values.phones
report.computers: other computers linked to this one, as one of values.computers
report.installAge: how long Bridge AI has been on this computer: week 1, 2-4 weeks, 5-12 weeks or 13+ weeks
report.daysActive: on how many days of the week something was counted, 0 to 7
report.activeTime: how long Bridge AI was in use that week (a window of it in front on this computer, with you typing, clicking, scrolling or touching it in the last two minutes; not phones), as one of timeRanges
report.openTime: how long Bridge AI was running that week, used or not, as one of timeRanges
report.features: the features on, each as one of its values under features (only those)
report.agents: the coding agents installed on this computer, each one of agents
report.counts: each counter below that isn't 0, as a bucket
report.nonce: random, new for each report, so a report sent twice is counted once; it says nothing about you or this computer

modelFamilies.about: How a model's name is counted (models.*, agents.model.*): the first family whose pattern (a regular expression, case ignored) fits the name, or other; never the name itself, which can be anything a provider or a model server calls it. For an answer, the name the provider says answered (a sign-in's own model) when it says one.

crashReports.about: Unless you turn off Send crash reports by themselves (at most five a day, the same crash once), and when you click Send to Bold Bridge on a crash's report, Bridge AI sends that report: the same text Report on GitHub shows, with names, folders, emails and keys taken out on your computer, and taken out again on the server.

report.kind: what crashed: ui (a part of the window), server, window (the desktop app's renderer) or gpu
report.channel: the update channel: stable, or early for Early Access (pre-releases, for testers with a code from the project)
report.tester: on Early Access, who the code is for: the first name or nickname the project gave its tester (letters, numbers, spaces, dots, apostrophes and dashes; 32 at most); otherwise null
report.title: the report's title, as Report on GitHub shows it
report.what: what happened, and what you wrote about what you were doing, when you send one yourself
report.details: its details: what crashed, the error and where in Bridge AI's code, the settings that change how it runs, and the last lines of its log, as Report on GitHub shows them

resumeWork.about: picking up agents' work after a restart

relay.about: the relay phones reach this computer through: your own, Bridge AI's, or none

location.about: a place set for the weather (only whether one is, never which)

appearance.about: light, dark or matching the computer

dayReport.about: Sent the day after each day Bridge AI ran, to the same server (/v1/day): which version it ran, the one it updated from that day if it did, its update channel and rollout bucket (and on Early Access, who the code is for), the OS and how it's installed, how many times it started, whether it crashed, and how long it was in use, as a range. With no ID, so each version's adoption and crash-free days can be counted, never followed.

report.day: the day, on the computer's calendar, e.g. 2026-11-04
report.app: Bridge AI's version at the end of the day
report.from: the version it updated from that day, or null
report.channel: the update channel: stable, or early for Early Access (pre-releases, for testers with a code from the project)
report.tester: on Early Access, who the code is for: the first name or nickname the project gave its tester (letters, numbers, spaces, dots, apostrophes and dashes; 32 at most); otherwise null
report.rollout: this computer's bucket for staged rollouts: a number from 0 to 99 picked once at random, shared with about one computer in a hundred, so a release out to 10% can be seen reaching buckets 0-9 first
report.starts: how many times it started, as one of buckets
report.crashed: true if its server, window or graphics stopped by itself that day
report.activeTime: how long Bridge AI was in use that day (as activeTime in a week's report: a window of it in front, used in the last two minutes), as one of dayTimeRanges

firstReport.about: Sent once, a couple of minutes after Bridge AI first runs on a computer (or the next time it runs, for a week, if it couldn't go), to the same server (/v1/first): that there's a new install, the day it was installed, its version, update channel, OS, chip and how it's installed. With no ID, so new installs can be counted the day they happen, never followed. Turning usage stats off before then means it never goes.

report.day: the day Bridge AI was installed, on the computer's calendar, e.g. 2026-11-04
report.channel: the update channel: stable or early
